voyage.name: Join for heritage walks
voyage.content: organised by two architects, these walks take you around various historic and architecturally significant areas of the city. Walks are organised on the third Sunday of every month (with a break from June through August for the monsoons) and the route varies each time. The walks last around 2 hours. Discounted rates for students and the physically challenged.

voyage.name: Banganga Festival
voyage.content: (Jan) The musical festival is organised by Maharashtra Tourism (MTDC) annually at Banganga Tank on Malabar Hill.

voyage.name: Elephanta Festival
voyage.content: (March) Organised by Maharashtra Tourism, the festival of music and dance at Elephanta Caves has in the past seen performances by renowned artists like Alarmel Valli, Sanjeev Abhyankar, and Ananda Shankar and traditional Koli dances as well as traditional food. 7PM-10PM (Ferries start at 4PM)

voyage.name: Kala Ghoda Festival
voyage.content: The arts and crafts festival is held in the last week of Jan or first week of Feb annually in the historic precinct of Kala ghoda in Mumbai.

voyage.name: Gateway of India
voyage.content: The landmark gateway was built in 1911 to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary to India. Built in the Indo-Saracenic style, the foundation stone for the Gateway of India was laid on 31 March 1911. The final design of George Wittet was sanctioned in 1914 and the construction of the monument was completed in 1924. This arch is the most recognisable symbol of the city. The structure is a basalt arch, 26

voyage.name: Sassoon Docks
voyage.content: One of the oldest docks in Mumbai and was the first wet dock constructed in the city. It is also one of the largest fish markets in the city. In 2017, street art transformed the fishing dock into an exhibition space.

voyage.name: Wellington Fountain
voyage.content: A small elegant marble fountain dating back to the 1860s.

voyage.name: Majestic Guest House
voyage.content: Once the majestic hotel it was designed by W.A. Chambers, who was also the designer of Mumbai's iconic Taj Mahal Hotel, Completed in 1909 it follows the Indo-Saracenic architectural style complete with domed minarets. Today it is known as Majestic Guest House and houses a government co-operative store and a hostel for Members of Legislative Assembly.

voyage.name: Waterloo Mansion
voyage.content: An Indo-Gothic style residential apartment. The ground floor houses several stores including cafes and restaurants.

voyage.name: Maharashtra Police Headquarters
voyage.content: The grand building dates back to 1876 and was built as a home for the seamen and was known as Royal Alfred Sailors Home. Built in Gothic style it was designed by Frederick William Stevens. The giant pediment at the centre of the building contains a statue of Neptune, the guardian of the seas. The sculptures on the other face of the building were designed by the students of J J School of Art under the guidance of John

voyage.name: Eros Cinema
voyage.content: A colonial-era cinema built in Art Deco style. The hall started functioning in 1938 and had a sitting capacity of 1204. It was closed down in 2016 for renovation, and was reopened in February 2024 with a 1,300-seater theatre and a 300-seater IMAX screen. All traces of the original auditorium were removed including the balcony, with only the large relief sculptures flanking the sides being incorporated.

voyage.name: Nariman Point
voyage.alt: नरीमन पॉइंट Narīman Pôiṇṭ; Manhattan of Mumbai
voyage.content: The area is on land reclaimed from the sea. Nariman Point is the business hub of Mumbai. However, with the change in economic conditions, many companies have shifted to other areas of Mumbai, like Parel, Worli, Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), Andheri-Kurla Road and Powai. There are many airline offices and luxury hotels here. It is widely regarded as the "Manhattan of Mumbai" and it boasts of a spectacular skyline and pr

voyage.name: Royal Opera House
voyage.content: The hub of social, artistic and cultural activity in Mumbai. The Opera House was inaugurated by King George V in 1911, but it was still under construction. It was finally opened to the public in 1916. It follows the Baroque style of architecture with a blend of European and Indian detailing. In 1917 it started showing films. The entire area near it came to be known as the Opera House. In 1993 the Opera House was clos

voyage.name: Taraporewala Aquarium
voyage.content: It has an exotic collection of marine and fresh water life. An interesting section demonstrates various stages in the growth of a pearl and also displays exquisite pearl, and mother-of-pearl jewellery.

voyage.name: Western Railway Headquarters
voyage.content: The massive grey and white sandstone building stands opposite Churchgate station and on the northwest corner of the Oval Maidan. The building was constructed in 1899. Although the Gothic architecture building dominates Mumbai's skyline on account of its location at a busy intersection it is often passed by unnoticed in the waves of humanity.

voyage.name: Babulnath Mandir
voyage.address: 16, Babulnath Rd, Charni Rd, Khareghat Colony, Malabar Hill
voyage.content: This temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is a well-known temple in south Mumbai. This temple is close to the beach and there is a climb of around 100 steps. It is also possible to take an elevator up to the temple.

voyage.name: Hanging Gardens
voyage.content: This terraced garden is visited on top of Malabar Hills. The park was laid out in 1881 by Ulhas Ghapokar over Bombay's main reservoir, probably to protect it from the contamination originating from the Parsi Tower of Silence. The park was renovated in 1921. The park is beautifully laid out with flower beds and hedges along with walkways. The park also provides a great sunset over the Arabian Sea.

voyage.name: Lok Bhavan
voyage.content: The official residence of the Governor of Maharashtra, appointed by the President of India, formerly the Raj Bhavan (राज भवन Rāj Bhavan). It was built upon the Bombay Castle, dating back to the 16th century, and was used in the British times as the Government House of the Bombay Presidency. Some parts of the complex are open to the public, including a museum dedicated to Indian freedom fighters located in a former Br

voyage.name: Tower of Silence
voyage.address: Dungar Wadi Rd, Simla Nagar, Malabar Hill
voyage.content: This is where the Parsis practice their famous burial custom of leaving bodies out in the open to be devoured by vultures. However, as the name hints, the site is within a tower where non-Parsis are not welcome, so there is nothing to be seen. There are several other Parsi (Fire) Temples in Mumbai. These are located at Churchgate, Princess Street, New Queen's Road, Gowalia Tank and Bandra. The Agiary, located at Fort

voyage.name: Walkeshwar Temple
voyage.address: Banganga Cross Ln, Teen Batti, Malabar Hill
voyage.content: This is a temple dedicated to the Hindu god, Shiva. According to legend, Lord Rama came here on his way to Lanka to reclaim his consort Sita, who was kidnapped by the Demon King, Ravana. The temple also has a tank called the Banganga. A quiet place amidst all the bustle.

voyage.name: Afghan Church
voyage.alt: अफगान चर्च Aphgān Carc; St. John's Church
voyage.hours: Daily dawn-dusk; the verger who lives next to the church will open the door if it is locked
voyage.content: This is an Anglican Church in Colaba, built by the British to commemorate the dead of the disastrous defeat in the First Afghan War of 1838. This church is believed to have hosted members of the White Brotherhood who believe that Lord Jesus visits them from the Cave of Light in the Dauladhar Mountains even today. The imposing edifice was constructed using locally available buff-coloured basalt and limestone. Inside i

voyage.name: Cathedral of the Holy Name
voyage.content: Cathedral of the Holy Name is the Catholic Cathedral of Mumbai. It is the headquarters of the Archdiocese of Mumbai. It is the seat of the Archbishop of Mumbai. The Mumbai (then Bombay) Catholic Christian life was centred around the Fort Chapel in Medows Street, which was constructed in 1767. At the beginning of the 20th century, the little Chapel was unable to accommodate the large congregation during the Sunday Mas

voyage.name: Chabad Nariman House
voyage.content: Chabad Nariman House, at the site of the 26/11 attacks, is home to the one-of-a-kind Jewish tour of tolerance and hope. Through visceral footage and displays, visitors witness the heart-wrenching story of the Murder of Rabbi and Mrs Holtzberg, the founders of the centre. The visitor faces the stark reality of modern-day terror and is challenged to assume personal responsibility for positive change. The centre is the

voyage.name: Harbour Cruise
voyage.content: If money is no object, rent Taj's private yacht (which has two sun decks and three bedrooms) for a cruise around the Mumbai Harbour.

voyage.name: Marine Drive
voyage.content: A 3.6-km-long C-shaped promenade along the coast of a natural bay. The six-lane road connects Nariman Point on the south to Girgaon Chowpatty on the north. It is popularly known as the Queen's Necklace, because when viewed during the night, preferably from an elevated spot, the lights on the road resemble the string of pearls in a necklace. There are walkways and benches along the bay and is a favourite hunt for both

voyage.name: Girgaon Chowpatty
voyage.content: This is the city's most famous beach, located at one end of Mumbai's most famous promenade. This is not a place to sunbathe, however. Go here to watch the crowds enjoying themselves and have bhel puri, as a moderately famous Hindi song asks you to. Chowpatty (caupāṭī) in Marathi means "beach", so you may hear people referring to other beaches suffixed with "Chowpatty" (for example, "Juhu Chowpatty"). But if they say

voyage.name: National Centre for the Performing Arts
Liberty Cinema
voyage.content: An Art Deco cinema built in 1947, the year of Indian independence. It has premiered various Bollywood films, most notably Mughal-e-Azam (1960).

voyage.name: Metro INOX Cinemas
voyage.content: An Art Deco multiplex opened on 5 June 1938.

voyage.name: Regal Cinema
voyage.content: This Art Deco cinema hall at SP Mukherjee Chowk dates back to 1933. Today, it is a multi-use building combining a cinema with shops at street level.

voyage.name: Colaba Woods
voyage.content: The garden has several facilities like a joggers' track, an amphitheatre, a readers' corner for street children, basketball courts, children's play areas and areas for relaxation. Photography and collection of plants and flowers are not allowed in the garden.

voyage.name: Cross Maidan
voyage.content: A large open place in South Mumbai. An old stone cross (crucifix) was built in the ground during Portuguese rule in the 16th century, hence the name. The ground is used for cricket in the dry season and association football during the monsoons. Near the southern end, the Mahindra United Club, a national-level club, has undertaken a lease of a small portion of the ground.

voyage.name: Kamala Nehru Park
voyage.content: The Kamala Nehru Park, named after the wife of Jawaharlal Nehru covers an area of 16,000 m² (4 acres) and is located atop Malabar Hills. The park has well-maintained lawns along with walkways. The shoe-shaped structure known as the Boot House is the park's prime attraction. The Boot House is inspired by the nursery rhyme "There was an old woman", where an old woman lived inside a shoe. The elevation of the park offer

voyage.name: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak Udyan
voyage.content: A memorial park dedicated to Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a freedom fighter, and part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio of Congress politicians in the 1900s.

voyage.name: Wankhede Stadium
voyage.content: Opened in 1975, this is the city's main cricket ground, and is the headquarters for the BCCI national governing body, for the Indian Premier League, and Mumbai Cricket Association. With a capacity of 32,000, it hosts Mumbai Indians in IPL.

voyage.name: Brabourne Stadium
voyage.content: An older cricket ground used for international matches.

voyage.name: Cooperage Football Ground
voyage.content: A football ground, and the home base of multiple Mumbai Football League clubs.

voyage.name: CR2 Mall
voyage.address: Barrister Rajni Patel Marg, Nariman Point
voyage.content: Houses the INOX multiplex.

voyage.name: Art & Design Book Store
voyage.content: Moderate choice of books from international publishers on various art topics. Some magazines.

voyage.name: Search Word
voyage.address: Metro House, S.B. Singh Rd, Apollo Bandar, Colaba Causeway

voyage.name: Oxford Bookstore
voyage.address: Apeejay House, 3, Dinsha Waccha Road, Churchgate

voyage.name: Colaba Causeway
voyage.content: It is filled with tourists and locals. It is a place where you will be able to find many authentic Indian souvenirs, antiques, carpets and chandeliers. But foreigners will have to be very careful, as all these stores are roadside stalls. What may seem a good price that the person has quoted to you, it will actually be a rip-off. Do not settle for anything more than one-fourth of the quoted price. If they refuse a pri

voyage.name: Bungalow eight
voyage.address: Inside Wankhede Stadium, North Stand, E & F Block, D Road, Churchgate
voyage.content: Very nice fashion shop, creative women's clothing from young Indian designers (Abraham & Thakore, for example); Bungalow Eight is a (very elegant) brand but also sells clothes from other designers. Furniture is also sold here. Prices are quite high.

voyage.name: Kashmir Oriental Carpet Showroom
voyage.address: 20 Crush Hall, the World Trade Centre, Cuffe Parade
voyage.content: One of the finest places where you can get exquisite hand-knotted carpets and rugs from Kashmir with genuine certification of authenticity. This store has an amazing range of breath-taking carpets in wool and silk with very reasonable prices and personalized service.

voyage.name: King's
voyage.content: High-quality tailors at affordable prices. The place to get a bespoke suit in Mumbai - no ready-to-wear clothes here! Sunil and Gopal, the two brothers that own the place, have good taste and commit themselves to fit your tailor-made suit perfectly. King's is also a shirtmaker and does sell some accessories like cufflinks, ties, and pocket squares. These are under the desk and you have to ask for them. King's suits a

voyage.name: Bademiya Kebab Restaurant
voyage.content: Eat on the road or in your car. Open until the early hours of the morning. The rolls are a favourite.

voyage.name: Baghdadi
voyage.content: Food is a mix of maintream Indian and Mughlai. Simple decor.

voyage.name: Crystal
voyage.content: Crystal is famous for its Parathas and North Indian fare. The food is very affordable and one will always find a line outside waiting to eat at Crystal.

voyage.name: Kailash Parbat
voyage.content: This is a basic restaurant, serving excellent vegetarian Indian food.

voyage.name: Martin's
voyage.content: Great Goan food. Order a drink quickly before your food is delivered to your table. Not for vegetarians.

voyage.name: The Bayview, Hotel Marine Plaza
voyage.content: This has a lunch, dinner, and midnight buffet worth trying. Also has a great view of Marine Drive and Malabar hill. Ask for the "Cafe Viennoise" and get extra chocolate flakes. It's not on the menu, so you have to ask the waiter for it.

voyage.name: Bhagat Tara Chand
voyage.content: Kalbadevi. Great Indian Curry and 'home food'. Must visit for Indian food lovers, but you have to walk a bit.

voyage.name: Cafe Basilico
voyage.content: off Colaba Causeway, near Strand cinema . This is not a budget restaurant, but it's not expensive either. Very popular with white immigrants who live in the city. Offers non-alcoholic drinks and coolers, Mediterranean-inspired food, and great dessert. Open all day. The rawas (local kind of fish) and the cheesecake is recommended.

voyage.name: Cafe Churchill
voyage.address: East West Court Building, Colaba Causeway, Apollo Bandar
voyage.content: Serves a mix of world foods (sandwiches, burgers, pasta, soups) in a very cramped location. The food is pretty good, especially the pasta. The desserts here are the best and one should not miss the Irish Baileys Chocolate Cake, which is highly recommended.

voyage.name: Cafe Mocha
voyage.content: It is a relaxed Sheesha restaurant serving heavy snacks. Very popular for dessert and coffee.

voyage.name: Cafe Royal
voyage.content: U.S. President Bill Clinton chose to eat here on his visit to India. Famous for sizzlers and other continental food.

voyage.name: Gable's
voyage.content: A restaurant that serves a good array of Goan food besides delicious Legs of Ham, Pork Chops and Steaks. Frequented by travellers, has a good British breakfast of ham, sausage, eggs and bacon.

voyage.name: Indigo Deli
voyage.content: Excellent food by the Indigo people at cheaper-than-Indigo prices. Very popular with locals and ex-pats for lunch and brunch on all days, so there can be quite a wait.

voyage.name: Leopold Cafe
voyage.content: This place requires no introduction and is a favourite with travellers and locals alike. Serves a mix of Indian, Chinese, Persian, and Continental Food. Also serves great breakfast round the clock; it is renowned for fresh fruit juices.

voyage.name: Mahesh Lunch Home
voyage.content: The most famous seafood place in the city. Definitely try the crab.

voyage.name: Moshe's
voyage.content: Mediterranean food. Extremely popular with locals, and a good, classy mid-range option.

voyage.name: Paradise
voyage.content: Serves Parsi food and is extremely popular amongst locals, especially those who have been eating here since they were kids. The place is family owned and one must try the chicken steak, the chicken dhansak, and a really nice chicken salad.

voyage.name: Pizza by the Bay
voyage.content: Serves a popular soup and salad buffet lunch. Frequented by locals, both families and young adults, in the evening. Decorated in Art Deco style.

voyage.name: Status
voyage.content: Very good vegetarian restaurant with a nice atmosphere. No meat nor alcohol here, but you won't miss it: the food is exquisite.

voyage.name: Golden Dragon
voyage.content: The upscale Chinese choice for locals and expats.

voyage.name: Lings Pavilion
voyage.content: High-end Chinese.

voyage.name: Tendulkar's
voyage.content: Cricket player Sachin Tendulkar's restaurant. A mix of continental and Indian cuisine including Sachin's favourite dishes.

voyage.name: Thai Pavilion
voyage.address: The Taj President, Cuffe Parade near Colaba
voyage.content: The only legitimate Thai restaurant in the city.

voyage.name: Trattoria
voyage.content: 24 hour coffee shop. Excellent pizzas. Can get extremely crowded on Sundays.

voyage.name: Wasabi
voyage.content: Japanese restaurant with a Nobu Chef.

voyage.name: The Bayview Bar
voyage.content: This bar has an arresting view of the Arabian Sea and the finest range of single malts and Habanos cigars. “George and Soft Rock Revolution” perform at the bar and sooth you with their charming renditions of jazz classics.

voyage.name: Bootlegger's
voyage.content: A small popular pub off Causeway. Reasonable drinks, ask for Jenga or Scrabble to play as drinking games.

voyage.name: Cafe Mondegar
voyage.content: Mondy's, as it's popularly called, serves excellent pitchers of Kingfisher, and at rock-bottom prices. Beer and wine are the only alcohols on the menu. Has a live jukebox and functions as a bar (beer and wine served) and restaurant. Food is a mix of Indian, Continental and Parsi, and the ambience is fun and low-key. Variety of TVs around showing sports games. Again extremely popular with local college kids. Suffers f

voyage.name: Gokul
voyage.content: It is frequented by anyone who wants an inexpensive drink served quickly. On the expensive side with an average drink costing ₹250 upwards. Boasts of a large wine collection and also serves superb fusion food. Excellent alcoholic Sunday brunch.

voyage.name: Indigo
voyage.content: An exclusive lounge and bar at Colaba causeway behind Taj Mahal Palace Hotel is a not to miss destination.

voyage.name: Opium Den
voyage.content: At Hilton Towers Mumbai. Serves a vast array of martinis, daiquiris, and home-infused vodkas. Quiet and convenient, this bar is a break from the ordinary. Open: 12:30PM-1:30AM.

voyage.name: Prive
voyage.hours: open til 3 on weekends unlike most Bombay nightclubs
voyage.content: One of the poshest and most popular nightclubs where you can watch the swish set prance around in their Blahniks and Ferragamos. Beware of long queues to get in, and a strict dress code and guestlist. Fights in this nightclub are a regular feature. Get a drink at the more chilled lounge Tetsuma next door before Prive.

voyage.name: Sports Bar
voyage.content: Come unwind at Sports Bar after haggling for trinkets on Causeway. Cheap (₹150 or so) drinks, pool table, and games on all screens.

voyage.name: Tavern
voyage.content: Shows music videos and is pretty packed, but don't go there if you don't like Linkin Park, etc.

voyage.name: Wink
voyage.content: A chill lounge at a nice 5-star hotel. Drinks are ₹400 up.

voyage.name: Woodside Inn
voyage.content: Across the road from Sports Bar, minus the sports. Cocktails are about ₹300, and the ambience is chilled. Good, reasonably priced food too.

voyage.name: Hotel Moti International
voyage.content: Clean, safe and quiet.

voyage.name: Hotel Marine Plaza
voyage.content: An Art Deco luxury hotel along the Marine Drive.

voyage.name: InterContinental Marine Drive
voyage.content: An IHG hotel.

voyage.name: The Oberoi Trident
voyage.content: Reserved luxury hotel on the waterfront.

voyage.name: President
voyage.content: An IHCL SeleQtions hotel.

voyage.name: Sea Green Hotel
voyage.content: An Art Deco hotel along the Marine Drive.

voyage.name: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel
voyage.content: The landmark hotel close to the Gateway of India, along with the Oberoi is one of the oldest five-star hotels in India. The building was commissioned in the Indo-Saracenic style by Tata and first opened its doors to guests on 16 December 1903. The builder was Khansaheb Sorabji Ruttonji Contractor who also designed and built its famous central floating staircase. The cost of construction was £250,000 (£127 million tod

voyage.name: Taj Mahal Tower
voyage.content: A wing of the Taj Hotel, this tower hotel was built on the site of the historic Green's Hotel, constructed as flats in 1890, and operated by Tata as a hotel from 1904 until its demolition to build the tower. Despite being owned by the same company that owns the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Taj Mahal Tower is relatively cheaper than the former.

voyage.name: Cave 1
voyage.content: Cave 1 is the largest and the grandest of the Elephanta Caves. The cave consists of a central large hall flanked by the Eastern and Western courtyard. The main hall is approachable from the north and is supported by colossal columns. The entrance is flanked by two sculptures on either side. On the left-hand side of the entrance is the statue of Yogishvara (Lord of Yogis) and on the right is Nataraja (Dancing Shiva).

voyage.name: Cave 2 - 5
voyage.content: Caves 2-5 of the caves are nothing spectacular but are only located next door, so it is advisable not to give it a miss. Caves 1 and 5 are unfinished caves with almost no ornamentations. Cave 3 has a grand entrance through a six-pillared entrance. It has a large porch and a shiva shrine guarded by damaged dvarapalas (gate guardians). Cave 4 lacks the grand entrance of cave 3 but otherwise, plans are similar with a sh

voyage.name: Cave 6 & 7
voyage.content: Caves 6 and 7 are located on the adjacent hill, which is known as Stupa Hill. One has to turn right after exiting from the gate of the main complex. It takes about 15 mins to reach the caves. The trail is not well marked and there are hardly any visitors. Cave 6, known as Sitabai’s temple cave, consists of three chambers with a portico. Interestingly, this cave was converted into a church by the Portuguese when the i

voyage.name: Stupas
voyage.content: Apart from the Hindu caves, Elphanta Island also houses two Buddhist stupas. In order to visit them, one has to continue beyond caves 6 & 7. One of the stupas is located on a hill top and the other on the coast. Both are extremely difficult to locate and are hardly visited by tourists.

voyage.name: Nature Walk
voyage.content: Bombay Natural History Society organizes nature tours in the Elephanta Island. The tour focuses on exploring the mangroves region of the island and includes bird watching and visiting caves, which serve as a bat dwelling. Cost ₹ 600 for members and ₹ 700 for non members, and includes ferry ride charges.

voyage.name: MTDC Chalukya Restaurant
voyage.content: Offers a fine spread of Indian food at a reasonable cost. The view of the sea from the MTDC restaurant is really pleasing

voyage.name: A Patil Flyover
voyage.content: Byculla is also known for Mumbai's first Y-shaped bridge built across Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Road which then splits further to go to Byculla East and West before the Clare Road intersection, thereby forming a Y shape when seen from the air. This was one of the oldest flyovers built in Mumbai.

voyage.name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Mumbai City Museum
voyage.address: 91 A, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Rd, Byculla East
voyage.content: Established in 1855 as a treasure house of the decorative and industrial arts. This museum houses a large number of archaeological finds, maps and historical photographs of Mumbai, clay models, silver and copperware and costumes. Its significant collections include a 17th-century manuscript of Hatim Tai. Outside the museum is the installation of the monolithic basalt elephant sculpture recovered from the sea, which o

voyage.name: Gloria Church
voyage.alt: Church of Our Lady of Glory; Portuguese: Nossa Senhora de Gloria
voyage.address: Sant Savta Marg, Mustafa Bazar, Byculla West
voyage.content: This is one of the oldest Roman Catholic churches in Mumbai built by the Portuguese Franciscans in 1632. The present structure dates back to 1913. The grey stone steeple of the church rises to a height of 160 feet. It is the tallest church steeple in Mumbai. The church follows the Gothic style of architecture with pointed arches. The church is 205 feet long and 65 feet broad and the interiors contain 5 altars.

voyage.name: Jerbai Baug and Rustom Baug
voyage.content: The two Parsi colonies where most of the Parsis of Byculla live.

voyage.name: Magen David Synagogue
voyage.content: Built in 1861 this is the first Bagdadi Jew Synagogue in Mumbai. The Bagdadi Jews started arriving in Mumbai (then Bomay ) in the early decades of the 19th century. During that time they are welcomed by the Bene Israel (Children of Israel) community to pray in their synagogue. By the middle of the 19th century the Bagdadi Jew community was large enough to have their own congregations along with their own synagogue. T

voyage.name: Magen Hasidim Synagogue
voyage.content: The Magen Hasidim Synagogue is the largest Bene Israel (Children of Israel) synagogue in Mumbai, it remains functional with a small congregation. The Bene Israel congregation of Mumbai (then Bombay) started in 1904. Initially they operated from makeshift facilities for their prayer and community service. Later a member of the community Benjamin Samson Dandoolkar established a prayer hall, which came to be known as Da

voyage.name: Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan
voyage.alt: वीरमाता जिजाबाई भोसले उद्यान Vīrmātā Jijābāī Bhosale Udyān
voyage.hours: 9AM–6PM (closed Wed); saplings are available from the Garden's Nursery. Thu–Tue 8AM–11AM and 3–5PM except on Sun and public holidays
voyage.address: Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Rd, Byculla East
voyage.content: The zoo was established during British times and named "Victoria Gardens". After India's independence, the zoo is renamed after Shivaji's mother Jijabai, and is popularly known as Rani Baug (queen's garden). The place is not really worth visiting as it has been called more of a prison for animals than a zoo in the modern sense.

voyage.name: Antilia
voyage.content: One of the most expensive homes in India, and one of the largest in the world, where billionaire Mukesh Ambani lives with his family. The 27-storey building is designed to withstand a magnitude-eight earthquake, and its design incorporates the lotus plant and the sun. The amenities inside the building include a 168-car garage, ballroom, 9 high-speed lifts, a 50-seat theatre, terrace gardens, swimming pool, spa, healt

voyage.name: Mani Bhavan Gandhi Sangrahalaya
voyage.hours: Museum daily 9:30AM-6PM, closed on 2nd and 4th Saturdays and public holidays. Library: Mon-Fri 9:30AM-6PM
voyage.content: The house where Mahatma Gandhi often stayed when he visited the city between 1917-1934. The two-storeyed structure standing on Laburnum Road is the city's pride. Gandhi's Museum & Library: once you enter the place, there is a library with a statue of the Mahatma where people offer their tributes. Then a staircase dotted with Gandhi's pictures depicting his life leads visitors to the first floor which has a big photo

voyage.name: National Museum of Indian Cinema
voyage.content: The museum houses artefacts, kiosks and digital sources of the history of Indian cinema.

voyage.name: Mumba Devi Temple
voyage.alt: Marathi: मुंबा देवी मंदिर Mumbā Devī Mandir, Gujarati: મુંબાદેવી મંદિર Mumbādevī Mandir
voyage.hours: Tue is the main day of worship
voyage.content: The temple dedicated to the city's patron goddess Mumbadevi, the local incarnation of the Devi (Mother Goddess). The city itself is named after the goddess. The first shrine dedicated to Mumbadevi is believed to have been built by a Koli fisherman in the 1st century BCE, on the site now occupied by CSMT. The temple is about six centuries old, believed to be the handiwork of Mumbaraka, a sadistic giant who frequently

voyage.name: Jama Masjid
voyage.content: It was constructed in 1802 on the tank. In the eighteenth century, this tank was situated in the midst of gardens and open land and belonged to a Konkani Muslim merchant trading in Goa, and Calicut, who, about 1778, agreed to the erection of a mosque on the spot, provided the tank was preserved intact. A one-story building was therefore erected over the tank and formed the original nucleus of the present Jama Mosque.

voyage.name: Dhobi Ghat
voyage.content: The famous open-air laundry place in Mumbai. Built in 1890, the washers in Dhobi Ghat work in the open to clean clothes and linens from Mumbai's hotels and hospitals. There are rows of open-air concrete wash pens, each fitted with its own flogging stone. The best time to visit Dhobi Ghat is early morning and early afternoon. While the dhobis are in action in the morning to take care of the washing load, the early aft

voyage.name: Haji Ali Dargah
voyage.alt: Marathi: हाजी आली दर्गा Hājī Alī Dargā, Urdu: حاجی علی درگاہ Hājī Alī Dargāh
voyage.content: The Haji Ali Dargah was constructed in 1431 in memory of a wealthy Muslim merchant, Sayyed Peer Haji Ali Shah Bukhari, who gave up all his worldly possessions before making a pilgrimage to Mecca. The Dargah Sharif is built on a tiny islet 500 m from the coast, in the middle of Worli Bay, in the vicinity of Worli. The edifice is a brilliant specimen of the Indo-Islamic style of architecture. The islet is linked to the

voyage.name: Mahalakshmi Temple
voyage.content: The temple dedidated to Mahalakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity is one of the most popular shrines of Mumbai. The temple contains images of the goddesses Mahalakshmi, Mahakali and Mahasaraswati. All three images are adorned with nose rings, gold bangles and pearl necklaces. The image of Mahalakshmi is shown riding a tiger and a demon (Mahishasur) in tandem. The compound of this temple contains several stall

voyage.name: Nehru Science Centre
voyage.content: A science museum, also contains the "Discovery of India", a show on India's History named for Jawaharlal Nehru's book. It is spread over a relatively large area and surrounded by greenery. Check the website for prices and timings of different shows. This is India's largest interactive science centre.

voyage.name: Tiphaereth Israel Synagogue
voyage.address: 92, K K Rd, Vaishali Nagar, Kasturba Quarters, Jacob Circle
voyage.content: The third Bene Israel (Children of Israel) synagogue of Mumbai. The original building dates back to 1896 and it was shifted to the larger present location in 1924, due to the efforts of community member Aaron Benjamin Kandlekar. In Kandlekar's honor for his generosity, the synagogue also became known as Kandlekaranchi Masjid or Kandlekar's Synagogue. The present building has undergone several renovation over years wi

voyage.name: Ferry Wharf
voyage.content: It used to be a harbour and the big and medium-sized boats were leaving for Goa and South Konkan. Now, small boats, dinghies, barges and ferries are operated and plying to Uran (in Navi Mumbai) and nearby areas. This is especially known for its wholesale fish market. It's also an immersion point during Ganesh Chaturthi.

voyage.name: Joseph Baptista Gardens
voyage.content: A park atop Bhandarwada Hill and offers a panoramic view of the Mumbai Harbour and the southern business district of the city. Beneath the gardens is a water reservoir, constructed between 1880–1884. The park is frequented by neighbourhood residents. It is mostly patronised by couples, joggers, senior citizens, and students who find peaceful corners to study. Cycas, ixora, musanda, bougainvillea, and hibiscus are som

voyage.name: Kuan Kung Temple
voyage.content: Mumbai once had a flourishing Chinatown, today the Kuan Kung Temple in Mazagaon is the only remaining trace of the once vibrant Chinese community of Mumbai. After the 1962 Sino-Indian War, most Chinese were viewed as traitors, and left town. The temple is housed in a two-storey building, with bright red entry doors. Wooden stairs lead to the first floor housing a shrine of Kwan Tai Kwon, the Chinese god of war. There

voyage.name: Mazagaon Court
voyage.content: Here in Tadwadi a B.I.T. Chawl's big Colony is also situated. This Tadwadi area is also famous for its dahi-handis. From this area, only the world’s most famous second manual tower forming Mandals are operating in Mumbai.

voyage.name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
voyage.alt: श्री स्वामीनारायण मंदिर Śrī Svāmīnārāyaṇ Mandir
voyage.content: It has a tri-spire structure and the idols installed are that of Laxminarayan Dev with Ghanshyam Maharaj, and Radha Krishna Dev with Hari Krishna Maharaj. In this temple, Radha Krishna is worshipped in the form of Radha Golokvihari as they are the residents of Goloka. It is a Shikharband Mandir and comes under the Laxminarayan Dev Gadi (Vadtal).

voyage.name: Raudat Tahera
voyage.content: This is a white-marble Fatemi shrine. The marble used in the mausoleum was quarried from the Chosira and Ulodi quarries of the famed Makrana quarries in Rajasthan, from where marble for Taj Mahal was quarried. - The mausoleum rests on 92 piles. The number 92 is significant in that it represents the Arabic isopsephical value of the name of Muhammad. The complete structure weighs 5000 tons. The mausoleum rises to a hei

voyage.name: Aga Khan's Maqbara
voyage.content: The mausoleum of Aga Khan I. Its architecture is said to have been inspired by the Taj Mahal.

voyage.name: Moghal Masjid
voyage.content: Built in an Iranian style in 1860 by a prominent Iranian businessman who had moved to Mumbai.

voyage.name: Gate of Mercy Synagogue
voyage.content: The oldest synagogue in Mumbai. It dates back to 1796 and is a Bene Israel (Children of Israel) Synagogue. For the first few decades, the Bene Israel Jews carried out their prayers in private places and burrowed halls but with a growing number of members they need a proper synagogue. A proper synagogue, which not only will serve as a physical place for prayer but also serve as a spiritual, educational, and social cen

voyage.name: Shaare Rason Synagogue
voyage.content: Constructed in 1843, the Shaare Rason Synagogue, literally meaning the "Gateway of Desire Synagogue" is the second oldest synagogue of Mumbai and belongs to the Bene Israel Jews. It is near the older Shaar Harahamin and with the construction of the new synagogue Shaar Harahamin Synagogue came to be known as the Old Synagogue and Shaare Rason the New Synagogue. The New Synagogue was constructed by voluntary contributi

voyage.name: Mahalaxmi Racecourse
voyage.content: An oval-shaped racecourse in Mumbai. The horse racing season starts in mid-November and ends in the last week of April. On the first Sunday in February, the Indian Derby is conducted annually and is attended by many of the city's glitterati. The Grandstand off the course is a designated heritage structure. The racecourse is the only helipad open for civilian use in Mumbai.

voyage.name: Nehru Planetarium
voyage.content: This is next door to the Nehru Science Centre and has some interesting shows. Over the years, it has grown into a centre for the scientific study of astronomy and space science. The planetarium is equipped with a Digistar 3 planetarium projector which was installed in 2003.

voyage.name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Indoor Stadium
voyage.content: An indoor sports arena with facilities for lawn tennis, badminton, billiards, table tennis, carrom, wrestling and futsal. Food options are limited though.

voyage.name: Bhuleshwar Market
voyage.content: for fruits and vegetables.

voyage.name: Breach Candy
voyage.content: Home to Premsons and Amarsons department stores.

voyage.name: Chor Bazaar
voyage.content: A colloquial term used to refer to a place selling stolen items. It consists of a number of interconnecting by-lanes with street vendors hawking a wide variety of items from antiques to shoes to car accessories etc. The place can be quite a surprise for the number and type of items on sale. A great place to spot bargains, and bargaining is a must. Shop with a keen eye: look out for fakes or second-hand items that are

voyage.name: Dava Bazaar
voyage.content: Famous for medical and scientific instruments and lab chemicals.

voyage.name: Heera Panna Shopping Centre
voyage.content: It's a popular shopping destination for locals and shops usually deal in imported goods and electronics.

voyage.name: Mangaldas Market
voyage.content: for silk and cloth

voyage.name: Mustafa Bazaar
voyage.content: A wholesale timber market is frequently visited by many from the city.

voyage.name: Vegetable Market
voyage.content: The Byculla Vegetable Market is the largest vegetable market in Mumbai even larger than Crawford Market. South side vegetable market (wholesale), north side fish & meat market.

voyage.name: Zaveri Bazaar
voyage.content: Best known jewellery market, all in one place.

voyage.name: Atria mall
voyage.content: One of the nicest, best maintained malls in the city. For upscale there's Mango, Nine West, Aldo, Promod, Guess, La Senza (all sold at slightly inflated prices in India). There's also your regular Nike, Reebok, Levi's, along with some cheaper local brands. Be sure to check out the Rolls Royce dealership next door.

voyage.name: Crossroads Mall
voyage.content: At the site of Crossroads, what used to be Mumbai's first mall. Nothing to write home about. Chinese Food: China Gate Restaurant (Heavily Indianized, spicy Chinese food. ₹300 per person).

voyage.name: Byculla Restaurant and Bakery
voyage.content: A typical Iranian restaurant that has been in business for just under a century.

voyage.name: Gallops
voyage.content: Continental and Indian food restaurant. It's expensive, but worth it for the ambiance, service, and food.

voyage.name: Mahalaxmi Race Course Restaurants
voyage.content: Mediterranean food (including kebabs, meats, seafood, and pizzas) at spectacular prices (expect to pay ₹1000-₹2000 a head with drinks). Beautiful, romantic ambiance, and if you sit inside you can see the horses stabled in the race course. Tote on the Turf: Uber-chic and trendy place, go just to check out the modern decor. Excellent Mediterranean food. Dishes between ₹500-₹1500, and an excellent bar too. Reservations

voyage.name: Oh! Calcutta
voyage.price: A meal for two would come to ₹800
voyage.content: A Bengali place which naturally means that it has an extensive seafood menu. It also has a good vegetarian selection.

voyage.name: Hype
voyage.address: 2A/1, Dr Annie Besant Rd, Atria mall, Worli
voyage.content: DJ Aqeel's nightclub.

voyage.name: Tote
voyage.content: Beautiful, chic restaurant and bar by the Indigo people. Cocktails are ₹300 up. Alcoholic Sunday brunch.

voyage.name: Apex Dormitory
voyage.address: S.M. Mansion, Mumbai Central (W) Dalal Estate

voyage.name: Seva Niketan Hostel
voyage.content: A solar-powered Jesuit-run men's hostel that has served as headquarters for various NGOs.

voyage.name: Hotel Rosewood
voyage.content: The location is somewhat inconvenient, but has a good restaurant called Oh! Calcutta.

voyage.name: Dharavi
voyage.content: The Dharavi slum is a breathtaking, overwhelming experience at the heart of this part of Mumbai, with a massive recycling industry, ultra-dense housing, and both poverty and wealth existing in close proximity. Seeing the slum firsthand is safer and easier under the auspices of a professional guide such as Fahim Vora, based in Dharavi. It is slowly being redeveloped into 10 towers in a so-called smart city by the Adan

voyage.name: Chaitya Bhoomi
voyage.alt: चैत्य भूमि Caitya Bhūmi; Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Mahaparinirvan Memorial
voyage.content: A Buddhist shrine and the cremation place of Dr B. R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution. It is a revered place of pilgrimage for Ambedkar's followers, who visit in millions annually on his death anniversary on 6 December. The structure is square in shape with a small dome divided into ground and mezzanine floors. In the square-shaped structure is a circular wall about 1.5 metres in height. In t

voyage.name: Portuguese Church
voyage.alt: Church of Our Lady of Salvation; Portuguese: Igreja da Nossa Senhora da Salvação
voyage.content: The oldest church in Mumbai, it was built by the Portuguese Franciscans.

voyage.name: Lokmanya Tilak Bridge
voyage.content: One of the oldest bridges in Mumbai, built-in 1923. This bridge is made entirely of granite and hard English-made metal. The bridge is an important connection between east and west Dadar. Approximately 10,000 cars use the bridge each day.

voyage.name: Mumbai Mayor's Bungalow
voyage.address: Swatantrya Veer Savarkar Marg, Dadar W
voyage.content: The official residence of the Mayor of Mumbai and the famous Sena Bhavan, headquarters of the political party Shiv Sena.

voyage.name: Rajgruha
voyage.content: The house of Dr B. R. Ambedkar. The ground floor of the three-storey building hosts a heritage museum. Ambedkar collected more than 50,000 books during his time at Rajgruha, which made it one of the largest personal libraries in the world at the time of his death.

voyage.name: Mahim Fort
voyage.content: Strategically located in Mahim Bay, the fort overlooks Worli to the south, Bandra to the north, and Mahim to the east. The origins of the fort are unclear, but it occupies a strategic location that has been frequently contested. The fort is in disrepair, suffering from administrative neglect, encroachment of slums, and exposure to tidal erosion. Large boulders are strewn on the sand and crevices as high as 3 metres (

voyage.name: St. Michael's Church
voyage.alt: सेंट मायकल चर्च Seṇṭ Māykal Carc; Mahim Church

voyage.name: Don Bosco Church and School
voyage.content: A very special and tranquil church. This is probably the most prominent landmark in this district.

voyage.name: Shree Marubai Gavdevi Mandir
voyage.content: Around the 1700s this area was called Marubai Tekdi Gaon, which is said was shortened to MaTunGa (Matunga). Marubai is the traditional Gaondevi (village Goddess) of Matunga whose small temple existed under a peepal tree at King's Circle.

voyage.name: Shri Siddhivinayak Temple
voyage.alt: श्री सिद्धिविनायक मंदिर Śrī Siddhivināyak Mandir
voyage.content: One of the most famous temples in Mumbai is a shrine to Lord Ganesha, the elephant-headed god who is said to be the destroyer of obstacles. Many devout Hindus walk from their homes to this temple barefoot, especially on Tuesdays, which is considered a special day. The queue to enter the temple stretches to eternity on Tuesdays, so visit some other day if you can.

voyage.name: Prabhadevi Temple
voyage.content: The temple with an idol representing goddess Prabhavati, dating back to the 12th century, even though the temple itself was built in 1715.

voyage.name: Sewri Fort
voyage.content: This is a fort in Mumbai built by the British at Sewri. Built in 1680, the fort served as a watch tower, atop a quarried hill overlooking the Mumbai Harbour. Up to the 18th century, Mumbai consisted of several small islands. In 1661, seven of these islands were ceded by the Portuguese to the British as part of the dowry of Charles II of England. The harbour proved eminently apposite, and the British planned to shift

voyage.name: Atal Setu
voyage.content: India's longest sea bridge, also known as Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link (MTHL). Named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, the bridge connects Sewri in Mumbai to Nhava Sheva in Navi Mumbai, across the Mumbai Harbour.

voyage.name: Sewri Flamingo Point
voyage.content: It has large areas of mudflats which are not only a safe habitat for flamingoes in winter but also have adequate food availability. A large number of flamingos reach along with their babies from their breeding area, Rann of Kutch, to Sewri every year. They arrive and stay between the month of October to March. Other bird species come to feed at the flats.

voyage.name: Sion Hillock Fort
voyage.content: In 1543, the Portuguese took possession of the islands of Bombay by force, naming one of them Sião after Mount Zion in Jerusalem. The Portuguese gave the Jesuit priests sole ownership of some of these islands. The Jesuits then built a chapel atop a conical hillock. The present-day fort was built by the British Governor of Bombay Gerard Aungier atop the hillock. Sion was then the boundary between British-held Parel Is

voyage.name: BEST Transport Museum
voyage.content: It features amateur mini models of BEST buses and the ancient trams.

voyage.name: Vitthal Temple
voyage.content: This is a 400-year-old temple built by Sant Tukaram who brought the idol from Pandharpur, home of the original temple of Lord Viththal. The temple is known as Prati Pandharpur (Pandharpur temple’s replica). One of the many one-day festivals in Mumbai has been held in this temple to devote Lord Vitthal on Ashadhi Ekadashi (According to Hindu calendar) in June/July.

voyage.name: Worli Fort
voyage.address: VB Worlikar Marg, Worli Tip, Worli
voyage.content: This fort was built by the British in Worli around 1675. The fort, built on Worli Hill, overlooked Mahim Bay at a time the city was made up of just seven islands. It was used as a lookout for enemy ships and pirates. The fort is completely in ruins today and a slum has enveloped the edifice. A bell tower peeps out of the ruins and the ramparts are used to dry clothes.

voyage.name: Palais Royale
voyage.content: The tallest building in India at 320 m with 88 floors. Surprisingly, the façades and interior of the skyscraper are still under construction to this day even though it is topped out way back in 2018. So you may have to wait before it is opened for the interior looks.

voyage.name: Maharashtra Nature Park
voyage.content: A small forested area with various species of butterflies.

voyage.name: Mancherji Joshi Five Gardens
voyage.content: Take a walk in the mornings.

voyage.name: Shivaji Park
voyage.alt: शिवाजी पार्क Śivājī Pārk; Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park
voyage.content: The park is named after the legendary 17th-century warrior king of the region, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. The park was created in 1925 by the Mumbai Municipal Corporation, in the days of the British Raj. This is the largest park in Mumbai, known for its political and social gatherings and as a cradle of the cricket religion. The walkway around the perimeter is crowded with people taking walks. The inner circumferen

voyage.name: Coastal Road Promenade
voyage.content: The newest promenade of Mumbai that runs along the city's Coastal Road from Worli to Malabar Hill. Unfortunately, there are no trees along the promenade, making the experience more Dubai-like.

voyage.name: Worli Seaface
voyage.content: A promenade in 2 parts.

voyage.name: Plaza movie theatre
voyage.address: NC Kelkar Road, Kasar wadi, Dadar West
voyage.content: This was damaged during the 1993 bomb blasts/riots. It has now reopened and remains one of the theatres in Mumbai that show Marathi movies.

voyage.name: Shivaji Mandir
voyage.content: Marathi plays are running in this theatre.

voyage.name: Dadar vegetable market
voyage.content: This was the heart of the city and was responsible for distributing vegetables across all of Mumbai. It is said that one can get all possible things in Dadar. It is also famous for its underworld.

voyage.name: Secondhand books
voyage.content: Dirt cheap prices, but many of them are pirated and the quality of paper is not very good.

voyage.name: Dadar (W) Flower Market
voyage.content: Visit early morning to see colourful and wholesale flower market in action

voyage.name: Dadar Emporium
voyage.address: NC Kelkar Rd, Dadar West, Dadar
voyage.content: For sarees and more.

voyage.name: Adacks
voyage.content: Reasonably priced shirts.

voyage.name: Benaras Silk House
voyage.address: Dr Baba Saheb Ambedkar Rd, Mahavir Nagar, Hindu Colony, Dadar and Ranade Road

voyage.name: Phoenix Palladium
voyage.content: One of the largest, most popular malls in Mumbai. You can find international designers and brands (from Burberry to Guess, Nike, Zara, Body Shop, etc.) to local brands and Indian designers. Check their website for the store listing. It can get extremely crowded on weekends. Also has a multiplex, food court, supermarket, restaurants and pubs. You can easily kill an entire day here if you choose. Multiplex, mall, food,

voyage.name: Guru kripa
voyage.alt: Supplier of samosas to almost all the cinema theatres in the city

voyage.name: Palladium Food Court
voyage.content: Veda Newest Indian restaurant: The food is good and decor bling. Spaghetti kitchen: decent Italian food. Try their thin-crust pizzas. Average ₹500 a head. Punjab Grill by Jiggs Kalra: Good Indian food at slightly inflated prices. Copper Chimney: The original Copper Chimney at Worli serves perhaps the best butter chicken in the city. Go for their chaat and buffet lunch, or simply for their smashing North Indian food (

voyage.name: Aaswad
voyage.address: Opp. Sena Bhavan, Shivaji Park, Dadar(W)

voyage.name: Diwa Maharashtracha
voyage.address: Kataria Marg, Takandas Kataria Marg, Dadar(W)

voyage.name: Aroma
voyage.content: Another traditional Punjabi restaurant for a quiet drink.

voyage.name: Classic
voyage.alt: Decent Pav Bhaji and Masala pav

voyage.name: Chinaman
voyage.content: Great Chinese resto at a purely reasonable rate.

voyage.name: Garnish
voyage.content: New place with Chinese, South Indian food.

voyage.name: Cafe Mysore
voyage.alt: The Oldest Udupi restaurant in Mumbai, serving South Indian food

voyage.name: 'Rama Nayak's Udipi Shri Krishna Boarding
voyage.alt: Lip-smacking South Indian thali served on a banana leaf

voyage.name: Aer
voyage.content: Poshest rooftop bar of the city, stunning decor and even better views of the city. Prices as to be expected from the Four Seasons.

voyage.name: blueFROG
voyage.address: D/2 Mathuradas Mills Compound, N.M. Joshi Marg, Lower Parel
voyage.content: A great place to eat some fusion cuisine, drink some creative or conventional cocktails and enjoy an awesome atmosphere. Live music Tuesday - Sunday with a great Brunch on Sundays. More than just a dining experience - you get the added bonus of listening to a great range of music: jazz, blues, funk, soul, afro/Latin electronic, club, rock, and folk.

voyage.name: Hard Rock Cafe
voyage.content: More club-like than most other Hard Rock Cafes worldwide. Packed with the post-office media crowd (usually between 20-30 years old), with a fair share of expats. Drinks ₹300 up. Thursdays band nights. Don't expect to get a table for a while if you go after 11PM. This place is usually packed with office folk on weekdays and plays older music. Expect your Zeppelin, Hendrix, REM, etc.

voyage.name: Shiro
voyage.content: It is a beautiful bar, modeled after Buddha Bar. Shiro does some fabulous sushi on one day and yet somehow can mess it up so bad on another. Retro nights on Fridays are always packed to bursting, and it usually stays open til 3AM on weekends. Cocktails are ₹300 up. Alcoholic Sunday brunch.

voyage.name: Hotel Ashray International
voyage.content: This is a two-star hotel close to Sion railway station.

voyage.name: Four Seasons
voyage.content: Mumbai's swankiest hotel. This is a five-star hotel and part of the Toronto-based Four Seasons luxury hotels and resorts. The hotel has 202 guest rooms and also offers India's highest rooftop bar. Restaurants at the hotel: café Prato & Bar, Pool Deck, San-Qi.

voyage.name: Hotel Midtown Pritam
voyage.content: This is a decently good hotel and is very close to Dadar station. - Here is the Pritam Da Dhaba: a traditional Punjabi restaurant with a very warm interior ideal for a quite drink

voyage.name: ITC Grand Central
voyage.content: This extremely posh hotel is also suitably expensive. Kebabs and Curries Restaurant: Spectacular Indian food. They serve the famous Delhi Bukhara curry at this ITC restaurant. Try their succulent kebabs, their thick-enough-to-cut dal bukhara, or their fantastic Indian breads. Expect to empty out your wallets at this place, each dish can be ₹1000.

voyage.name: Bandra Fort
voyage.address: at the tip of the Bandra promontory, Bandstand Rd, Bandra W
voyage.content: Built by the Portuguese in 1640 to mark the southernmost tip of the mainland (i.e. Salsette Island). Not many remains. It was built as a watchtower overlooking Mahim Bay, the Arabian Sea and the southern island of Mahim. Castella de Aguada has been featured in several Hindi films.

voyage.name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount
voyage.address: Mount Mary Church Rd, Bandra W
voyage.content: This is probably Mumbai's most famous church, a Roman Catholic Basilica. The basilica stands on a hillock, about 80 metres above sea level overlooking the Arabian Sea. - A fair held annually on the Sunday following September 8 (which is the Feast of Our Lady of the Mount) draws visitors from all religions. - The chapel of Mount Mary, was built around 1640. The chapel was destroyed in 1738 by the Marathas during their

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady of Mount Carmel
voyage.content: A Jesuit church in Bandra. It was established in 1894 on the land given by Mount Mary and St. Andrew's churches.

voyage.name: Ghanteshwar Temple
voyage.content: A Hanuman temple known for being chock-full of bells (घंटा ghaṇṭā), including the ones donated by devotees. The local belief is that if people pray for Hanuman for something, and the request is granted, they must contribute a bell there.

voyage.name: Kadeshwari Devi Temple
voyage.content: A Devi temple behind the Bandra Fort at Land's End.

voyage.name: Khar Danda
voyage.content: A fishing village on the north-western coast of Bandra, inhabited by Koli and East Indian Catholics. This village is famously known for its quaint fishing business, modern piers, colorful fishing vessels, and traditional homemade soft liquor extracted from fermented fruits.

voyage.name: Ramakrishna Mission, Khar
voyage.content: It organises an annual fest between October and December, and is widely attended for its mix of eclectic stalls selling cultural wares, clothes, religious and spiritual books, devotional music and eateries.

voyage.name: St. Andrew's Church
voyage.content: It is one of the oldest churches in Mumbai, It was built by the Portuguese Jesuits in 1575. It was the only church in Bandra until the first quarter of the 17th century.

voyage.name: National Stock Exchange
voyage.content: The other stock exchange of Mumbai since the BSE at Dalal Street, Fort. NSE was incorporated in 1992 to bring about transparency in the Indian equity markets.

voyage.name: Bandra-Worli Sea Link
voyage.content: One of the longest sea bridges in India, connecting Bandra to Worli. It has reduced the travel time between Bandra and Worli during peak hours from 20 to 30 minutes to 10 minutes. Two-wheeler motor vehicles, three-wheeler motor vehicles and pedestrians are prohibited to access the bridge. You should also avoid cycling on the bridge since police officers often treat motorless bikes as motor vehicles and apply hepty fi

voyage.name: Juhu Beach
voyage.content: On the shores of the Arabian Sea, the beach stretches for six kilometres up to Versova. The short, rocky formations make up the Juhu Beach unlike the Marina Beach in Chennai that is primarily sandy. It is a tourist attraction throughout the year and is also a destination for shooting films. The beach generally gets more crowded on weekends and public holidays. The food court at its main entrance is known for the stre

voyage.name: Jogeshwari Caves
voyage.content: Consisting of a single cave dating back to 520 to 550 CE.

voyage.name: Mahakali Caves
voyage.address: Mahakali Caves Rd, Sunder Nagar, Andheri East
voyage.content: The complex consists of 19 rock cut caves constructed between 1st century BCE to 6th century CE. The caves are divided into two parts. South East section has 15 caves while the North West section has 4 caves. Kondivite (Cave 9) is the largest cave and the only one to house a chaitya. Cave 9 also houses several sculptures of Buddha but the figures are mutilated.

voyage.name: Gurdwara Guru Nanak Punjabi Sabha Chakala
voyage.content: One of the few gurudwaras in Mumbai.

voyage.name: Our Lady of Egypt Church
voyage.content: Another pre-British Catholic church in Mumbai. It was founded in 1606 and it celebrated its 400th anniversary in 2006.

voyage.name: Sacred Heart Church
voyage.content: A Catholic church that began as a small chapel around 1850 for the original East Indian villagers who were served by the St. Andrews Church in Bandra. Every Sunday, a priest from Bandra would come to Santacruz and offer mass for Catholics residing in the traditional village. In the early 20th century, many Catholics from Goa, Mangalore and Kerala began migrating to Bombay. These people settled in Santacruz since Bomb

voyage.name: St. John the Baptist Church
voyage.content: An abandoned church inside an electronics complex. It was built by the Portuguese Jesuits in 1579, and was opened to public worship on the feast of John the Baptist. It also had an attached graveyard. The church was abandoned in 1840 after an epidemic hit the area. Fr. José Lourenço Pais, the then-Vicar of Kondivita transferred the church to the nearby Marol village. The baptismal font, pillars and altars were transf

voyage.name: Juhu Aerodrome
voyage.content: A general aviation airfield. It also hosts the Bombay Flying Club and several executive and light aircraft. The airfield is featured in various climax scenes of Indian films.

voyage.name: Mehboob Studio
voyage.content: This is where some of the famous Bollywood films of yester-year were made.

voyage.name: Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre
voyage.content: A performing arts and multi-disciplinary cultural and exhibition space. It was founded by a daughter of billionaire Mukesh Ambani to "preserve and promote Indian arts".

voyage.name: Prithvi Theatre
voyage.address: 20 Janki Kutur Juhu Church Road, Juhu
voyage.content: Prithvi Theatre has shows everyday except Mondays and hosts an annual summertime programme of workshops and plays for children, the Memorial Concert on 28 February, an annual Theatre Festival in November, and many partnership programmes promoting language, poetry, international cinema & documentaries, and performing arts, which are free to the public.

voyage.name: Bandra Talao
voyage.content: A 200-year-old lake, constructed by an unknown rich Konkani Muslim.

voyage.name: Jogger's Park
voyage.content: A 400 m long seaside jogging track. It features a mud strip for running and two paved tracks for walking or jogging.

voyage.name: Bandstand Promenade
voyage.content: A 1.2 km long walkway along the sea on the west side of Bandra. It is simultaneously a popular hang-out spot, a jogging track, a park and also a lovers' point. Visible along the promenade are expensive bungalows and flats, some of which belong to Bollywood movie stars. Towards the Land's End side of the promenade is an amphitheatre. It serves as a venue for the Mumbai Festival, Celebrate Bandra and other events inclu

voyage.name: Carter Road Promenade
voyage.content: This is a 1.25 km long walkway along the sea on the west side of Bandra. Because of its sea-facing location in Bandra, the promenade has some high-priced residential localities.

voyage.name: Andheri Sports Complex
voyage.content: A multi-purpose sports facility. The sports complex has an Olympic-size swimming pool, a diving pool with 4 diving levels and an association football stadium known as Mumbai Football Arena.

voyage.name: Hill Road
voyage.content: Shopping area lined with malls, stores, shops, and hawkers selling branded (and cheap) export surplus clothes.

voyage.name: Infinity Mall
voyage.content: Good place for shopping at Andheri (West) Linking Road. Includes movie theatres, as well as Landmark, one of the best book, music, and DVD stores in Mumbai.

voyage.name: Jio World Drive
voyage.content: A large shopping mall run by Mukesh Ambani's conglomerate Reliance Industries. The mall has fashion shops, restaurants, cafés, a drive-in theatre and also India's first Apple Store.

voyage.name: Linking Road
voyage.content: The third largest shopping district in India in terms of revenue and footfalls, with world-class stores like Esprit, Tommy, Mango, Nine West, Benetton, etc.

voyage.name: Peshawari
voyage.content: Its sister restaurant Bukhara in Delhi has been recognised as the best Indian restaurant around the world. Try tandoori jhinga, the kebab platter, sikandari raan (leg of lamb), and mangoes and ice cream (only during summers), Kebab Corner (Hotel Intercontinental), Copper Chimney (Worli) Khyber (Kala Ghoda), and Kareem's Malad Link Road in Malad W.

voyage.name: Rasoee Veg Kitchen
voyage.content: Serves a sumptuous Gujarati Thali at the upper level. The waiters hover around you insisting that you eat more. At the end of meal, your hands are washed in a special vessel by pouring water out of a jar that wouldn't be out of place in a Maharaja's palace.

voyage.name: Little Italy
voyage.content: Run by Chef Giovanni, Little Italy is vegetarian and serves some great pasta a la puttanesca. Has valet parking.

voyage.name: Little Italy
voyage.address: 3-4 Morya Estate, Andheri - Oshiwara New link Rd
voyage.content: Little Italy has gone the chain restaurant way and has opened a franchise in Andheri West. The same great food can be had here too.

voyage.name: Thai Ban
voyage.address: Shop Number 8, Gaspar Enclave, Pali Naka Bandra
voyage.content: A great, suburban favourite, this restaurant is wonderful value. Authentic Thai food with loads of coconut milk. Tiger prawns in spicy lemon sauce, squid with nakaching, and chicken satay are all memorable, and often superior to more upmarket competitors.

voyage.name: Yoko's Sizzlers
voyage.address: 10/11, West View, S.V. Road, Near Akbarally's, Santacruz(West), 54
voyage.content: Serves excellent sizzlers.

voyage.name: Palm Grove
voyage.content: Ramada Plaza Palm, Juhu Beach, Mumbai +91 22 2611 2323, is a place that offers surprisingly great ambiance and some really economical beer. The service is good and they have a live band in the evenings (7PM-11PM). Happy hour (about 25% discount on food and beverage) extends up to 7PM. The crowd is fairly decent and includes a fair sprinkling of Europeans in the evenings. (Expect to spend about ₹120 ($3) for a beer (+

voyage.name: Aurus & Vie
voyage.content: Two separate bars facing the sea with a restaurant too. Great place for a nice drink after dinner.

voyage.name: Enigma
voyage.content: Great place for some Bollywood music and glance of Bollywood stars.

voyage.name: Firangi Pani
voyage.content: Reasonably priced, drinks, great ambience, good rock music. Ladies drink free on Mondays and Wednesdays.

voyage.name: Hawaiian Shack
voyage.content: Cheap drinks, good rock music. Four floors including a rooftop. Dance music on upper floors.

voyage.name: Mumbai Times Cafe
voyage.content: Cheap drinks, good rock music, very average food.

voyage.name: On Toes
voyage.content: One of the cool hang outs in Juhu area which plays good music. It is not cheap but a great place to have some drinks and relax.

voyage.name: Poison
voyage.alt: It's a great place to get a taste of Bollywood music

voyage.name: Toto's Garage Pub
voyage.address: 30, Lourdes Haven Pali Junction, Bandra West 400 050, (Off Pali Market)
voyage.content: Cheap drinks, good rock music

voyage.name: Zenzi
voyage.content: Sees a lot of the expatriate crowd apart from models and filmmakers. Drinks aren't cheap and the service is slow, but the place is always buzzing.

voyage.name: Aurus and Vie
voyage.content: Classy lounges with bay views.

voyage.name: China House
voyage.content: Along with Prive, perhaps the city's poshest, hardest-to-get-into nightclub. Fabulous interiors, drinks from ₹ 500, and upscale crowd. Strict entry rules, no stags, couples ₹ 1500.

voyage.name: Enigma
voyage.content: The Bollywood club, for both the music and the crowd. Go star-gazing. Expensive.

voyage.name: Olive
voyage.content: Usually a lounge-y restaurant, has bar nights on Thursday.

voyage.name: Poison
voyage.content: One of the more popular city nightclubs.

voyage.name: Zenzi
voyage.content: Decent music, good crowd, expensive drinks. No entry charge.

voyage.name: Hotel Orritel West
voyage.content: This is a reasonably good budget hotel with airport transfers, a 24-hour coffee Shop, a garden restaurant, and conference and banquet halls.

voyage.name: Hotel Regent
voyage.address: Ramakrishna Mandir Rd, Kondivita, Andheri E
voyage.content: This is a reasonably good budget hotel.

voyage.name: Tunga International
voyage.address: B- 11 M.I.D.C, Central Road, Opp Mahakali Caves Road Andheri E

voyage.name: Hotel Airlines International
voyage.address: Yoga Institute Rd, Prabhat Colony, Santacruz E

voyage.name: Lotus Suites
voyage.address: Andheri Kurla Road, International Airport Zone, Andheri (E)

voyage.name: Mirage Hotel
voyage.address: International Airport Approach Road, Marol, Andheri East
voyage.content: Complimentary buffet breakfast with vegetarian and non-vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Ramada Plaza Palm Grove
voyage.content: Juhu Beach, Mumbai. Complimentary Buffet breakfast.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Mumbai
voyage.content: Five star lifestyle complex. Has two outdoor pools and a spa.

voyage.name: JW Marriott Mumbai Juhu
voyage.content: A 20-minute drive from the airport, near Juhu beach, offers a great view of the Arabian sea.

voyage.name: Ramada Plaza by Wyndham Palm Grove
Taj Lands End
voyage.address: Byramji Jeejeebhoy Rd, Bandstand, Bandra W

voyage.name: Powai Lake
voyage.content: A man-made lake that used to be the city's water supply, now a tourist destination. Although it isn't really that spectacular, the lake is bordered by the skyscrapers of the Hiranandani Gardens, and there are many crocodiles on the lakeside. It is best viewed from the IIT Bombay campus.

voyage.name: Thane Creek
voyage.content: One of the two creeks that separate Mumbai from the rest of India. It is known for various flamingo species, especially greater flamingoes and lesser flamingoes. Alongside the flamingoes, 167 species of birds and small mammals like golden jackals are also present.

voyage.name: Bail Bazaar and Sindhi Camp
voyage.address: Lal Bahadur Shastri Rd, Bail Bajar, Sakinaka
voyage.content: Is an area in the northern end of Kurla West (populated by mostly Sindhi's, Kanojia's and Malwanis)

voyage.name: Hanuman Temple
voyage.content: It has gone through a major renovation. In the good old days, it has a rural charm with a huge tree in the backyard.

voyage.name: Holy Trinity Church
voyage.content: One of the numerous Portuguese-era churches in suburban Mumbai, and the major one in the Central Suburbs.

voyage.name: Rajawadi Garden
voyage.address: Rajawadi Road Number 3, Rajawadi, Ghatkopar East
voyage.content: This is the first municipal garden in it is a place which morning walkers have been using since a pretty long time.

voyage.name: Sanyas Ashram
voyage.content: As the name suggests, it is a transit point for the Sanyasis (the Hindu monks). It has the idols of all the major Gods and Goddesses

voyage.name: Sindhu Wadi
voyage.content: This is a landmark arch with the words "Sindhu Wadi" and a big clock.

voyage.name: Acres Lifestyle Club
voyage.content: For non-members also. Activities like Bowling, Pool, Video Games etc at their gaming arcade. They also have go-karting, cricket etc

voyage.name: Bombay Presidency Golf Club
voyage.content: One of the oldest and most famous golf clubs in Mumbai. It was built in 1927 on of reclaimed marsh.

voyage.name: Chembur Gymkhana
voyage.content: For members only. 79 ft. x 45 ft. Swimming Pool, Two cafeterias by different contractors, gymnasium, tennis courts, indoor badminton, Has a 62,957 sq.ft (1.445 acres) ground used for cricket and seasonal wedding parties.

voyage.name: Hakone Games Park
voyage.content: Hakone is a combination of Special Sports, Entertainment and Leisure at Powai. It is one of the most desirable attractions in Mumbai. The variety of attractions spanning rides and aqua pad boats for children as well as go-karting, paintball, and dashing cars for adults are as popular as the mini train ride for infants.

voyage.name: IMAX dome theater
voyage.address: Bit outskirts on Eastern Express Highway, Near wadala truck terminus
voyage.content: The world's largest IMAX dome theater, in 2008.

voyage.name: Old Machi (fish) Market
voyage.address: RB Kadam Road area, Bhatwadi, Ghatkopar (West)
voyage.content: It was once called horseshoe valley, because of the horseshoe-shaped hills surrounding the area.

voyage.name: Huma Mall
voyage.content: Here is the Hotel Sheetal Samudra known for its fine seafood, a very nice open air restaurant Sheesha with nawabi cuisine and hukkas, also is a one stop shop for finest Factory outlets, 6 Screen BIG Cinema Multiplex, the Hotel Meeting point one of the best restaurants around the area, and Muthoot Finance known for its Gold Loans, Investments, Gold Coins, Money Transfer, Insurance, Foreign Exchange, Tours & Travels et

voyage.name: Nirmal Lifestyles Mall
voyage.content: There is Shoppers Stop store, a McDonald's, and cafe including Manchester United Cafe Bar, Cafe Coffee Day, apart from six screen PVR multiplex.

voyage.name: Phoenix Marketcity
voyage.content: One of the biggest malls in Asia.

voyage.name: R City Mall
voyage.content: It has over 194 shopping stores, over 66 food outlets, 10 entertainment areas, 3 ATM facilities, 13 service areas and an INOX cinema hall.

voyage.name: R-Mall
voyage.content: The oldest mall in suburban Mumbai, opened in 2003.

voyage.name: K-star Mall
voyage.content: Has a Food Bazaar and a multiplex cinema

voyage.name: Saffron Spice
voyage.price: ₹221 (for the buffet, exclusive of VAT. An à la carte meal without alcohol would probably come to ₹500 per person all inclusive.)
voyage.content: An "Indian specialty restaurant" and one of the very few mid-range restaurants in the Powai area. The restaurant has received fairly decent reviews and the food has been appreciated for its variety. But it is extremely crowded during lunch and the staff will encourage you to choose the buffet. The lunch buffet is indifferent and the service is lousy, so you will have your rotis cold. It has a well-stocked bar and off

voyage.name: Hotel Rajhans
voyage.content: Provides complimentary continental breakfast and has a restaurant "Ornament" and a wine bar.

voyage.name: Hotel Pearl
voyage.address: 19th Road Corner, D.K Sandu Marg, Chembur

voyage.name: Tiara Dormitory
voyage.address: Bldg no 13 , 2nd floor, station road, opposite Aakash cinema lane, above Swastik Bhuvan, Kurla West

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Mumbai International Airport
voyage.address: Sakinaka Junction, Andheri Kurla Rd, Andheri E
voyage.content: Modern hotel with quality rooms. Good western and Indian breakfast. Local area and view from room not attractive but view from pool on roof is impressive. Less than 15 minute drive (can call hotel to arrange pick-up, although can be fee) from Terminal 2.

voyage.name: Marriott Executive Apartments Lakeside Chalet
voyage.content: Two and three bedrooms.

voyage.name: Taj The Trees
voyage.address: Off, Eastern Express Hwy, Pirojshanagar, Vikhroli East
voyage.content: One of the many Taj hotels in Mumbai, run by the same company behind the original Taj Mahal Palace.

voyage.name: Ambu Island
voyage.content: An island near Madh Island, accessible during low tide across an isthmus. There's a church and a Hindu temple, as well as a small lighthouse.

voyage.name: Film City
voyage.content: The film studio complex that serves as the venue for many shootings for Bollywood. Since 2014, it has started guided tours taking you to historical and live shooting sets.

voyage.name: Mandapeshwar Caves
voyage.address: Laxman Mhatre Rd, Mandapeshwar, Dahisar W

voyage.name: Church of St. Bonaventure
voyage.content: A 16th century Portuguese church on the beach. The annual Erangal Feast in January, attracts thousands of people of all faiths for the tribute to the church's namesake.

voyage.name: Madh Fort
voyage.hours: It is under control of the Indian Air Force as it is located close to an Indian Naval base and permission is needed for accessing it.
voyage.content: This is a small fort. It was built by the Portuguese and lost it in February 1739 during the war against Maratha empire. It is secluded and difficult to reach. The fort was built by the Portuguese as a watchtower in the 17th century. It offers a strategic view of the coastline and guards the Marve Creek. Its external façade is intact but internally it is dilapidated. Madh Island fort is surrounded by local fishermen'

voyage.name: Global Vipassana Pagoda
voyage.alt: विश्व विपस्सना पॅगोडा, Viśva Vipassanā Pêgoḍā
voyage.content: Opened in 2008, it is the largest mediation hall in the world. Built out of gratitude to the Vipassana teacher Sayagyi U Ba Khin, the pagoda is said to be a monument of peace and harmony.

voyage.name: Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Church
voyage.content: Built in 1544, ten years after the Bombay-Bassein coastal tracts were ceded by the Sultan of Cambay, Bahadur Shah, to Portugal by the Treaty of Bassein.

voyage.name: Temple of Sai-Dham
voyage.address: Mahatma Gandhi Rd, Sukarwadi, Borivali East
voyage.content: There are many Hindu deities worshipped under one roof.

voyage.name: Vazira Naka
voyage.content: This is very well known for Siddhivinayak Temple of Lord Ganesh (Swayambhu).

voyage.name: Essel World
voyage.price: Essel World ₹800, Water Kingdom ₹900, combined ticket ₹1200. discounted tickets also
voyage.address: Global Pagoda Road, Gorai Creek, western coast of Borivali
voyage.content: It is an amusement park. There are 34 major rides not to include the coin operated games & a mini club. There are over 30,000 specimens in their botanical gardens and 79 rides and slides & Essel World attracts almost 1.8 million visitors each year.

voyage.name: Prabodhankar Thackrey Auditorium
voyage.content: Where a variety of dramas, plays are scheduled (in Gujarati, Hindi, Marathi & also in some south Indian languages).

voyage.name: Veer Savarkar Udayan Garden
voyage.content: an ideal place for all which have facilities like jogging track, boating area, kids play garden, skating, etc.

voyage.name: Manori Beach
voyage.price: ₹2.50 per person for the ferry, additional charges for vehicles
voyage.content: This is a small beautiful island with nice beaches, but dangerous for swimming. The beach on the northern side is cleaner. This is a nice place to spend the weekend though. Apart from beachside shacks, there are two resorts in Manori designed like Spanish villas. It has a couple of hotels (see under Sleep) Make sure to try the seafood here. Also be sure to book in advance, as the rooms get filled up, especially over

voyage.name: Marvé Beach
voyage.content: Movement on Marvé Beach is restricted due to its narrow width as well as the presence of the Indian Naval base, INS Hamla. The beach is not safe for swimming due to the presence of very swift currents and sinking sand. This is also a good spot for fishing. You will find local boys with strings in hand. They use bait like shells, shrimp and earthworms to lure fish into their hooks. It is a good pass time and hobby.

voyage.name: Gorai Beach
voyage.content: On holidays the beach is full of visitors and locals. Plenty of accommodation options are also available at Gorai Beach.

voyage.name: Growels 101
voyage.address: Akurli Rd, off Western Express Hwy, Kandivali East
voyage.content: Four-level shopping centre.

voyage.name: Infiniti Mall
voyage.content: There are various areas for shopping, multiplex theatre complex, entertainment & games, food court, recreational area, multipurpose hall/ unit, offices, storage, parking, services, etc.

voyage.name: Inorbit Mall
voyage.content: The largest mall in Mumbai. There are movie theatres in the mall and various international brand stores. You can also use the mall property for your morning walks at no cost. Avoid going on weekends and holidays, especially in the evening.

voyage.name: Oberoi Mall
voyage.address: Dindoshi, Goregaon East, Oberoi Garden City
voyage.content: It offers the upmarket shopper over 500 brands under one roof.

voyage.name: Tourist Resort
voyage.address: Vairala Talao, Gorai Beach, Uttan Road, Borivali West
voyage.content: Working hours: M-Sa 7AM-11PM

voyage.name: Blue Balerina
voyage.address: Erangal Beach, Madh Marve Road, Malad West, Malad West, Marve Rd, Chikuwadi, Malad West

voyage.name: The Resort
voyage.address: 11, Madh-Marve Rd, Aksa Beach, Malad W
voyage.content: One of the most popular resorts in the city. The rooms are warmly decorated with Wi-Fi access, flat-screen TVs, views of the sea, plush bathrooms, a restaurant, a coffee shop and a lagoon-style outdoor swimming pool.

voyage.name: The Retreat
voyage.content: A five-star beach facing hotel.
